metadata.title: A to Z reading intervention for struggling second graders: a difference-in-differences quasi-experimental evaluation

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study evaluates a school-based reading intervention in Portugal using a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences design with intervention and control groups drawn from the same local school context. The analytic sample consists of 1009 second-grade students (182 intervention; 827 control) who could read at least five words per minute at baseline, with outcomes measured at three evaluation moments (September, January, May). The manuscript does not report the use of complex survey weights or any ILSA-style sampling weights; instead, it relies on clustered standard errors (clustered at the individual level) and student fixed effects within OLS difference-in-differences regressions. Because no survey-weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) is mentioned, the results should be interpreted as effects within the study’s implemented sample rather than population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the study does not use ILSA/PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS achievement scales with PV-based scoring; instead, it uses directly observed oral reading fluency outcomes (words per minute, reading accuracy, and reading expressiveness) collected in the intervention context. Missing-data handling is not reported because the paper describes attrition and exclusions (e.g., students unable to read text were excluded) but does not specify a formal missing-data procedure (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion rules or imputation) for missing outcome or covariate values.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were 1009 second-grade students (boys 51.3%, aged 7–8) from public schools in Portugal, drawn from 108 classrooms across 73 schools that volunteered to receive the program. Students were assigned to the intervention group if they met both (a) a median threshold on the Hong-Kong Learning Difficulties Behaviour Checklist subscales (reading comprehension, spelling/dictation writing, written expression) and (b) an oral reading test speed of ≤30 words per minute; tutor-teachers then worked with small groups (max three students per class) during class time. Students who could not read text were excluded from analysis because reading speed, accuracy, and expressiveness could not be measured. Outcomes were evaluated at three moments (September baseline, January post-intervention, May end-of-year), and attrition occurred (10.34% intervention; 20.71% control).

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIRLS 2016 the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Reading Literacy, finding that This study evaluates the “A to Z” (A to Z) reading intervention for struggling second graders in Portugal using a difference-in-differences quasi-experimental design with student fixed effects. The analytic sample includes 1009 second-grade students (182 intervention; 827 control) from 73 schools, with outcomes measured at three evaluation moments across the school year (September, January, May). Four reading-related dependent variables were analyzed: words per minute (WPM), log(WPM), reading accuracy (percentage correct), and reading expressiveness (ordinal 1–5). The intervention produced positive and statistically significant DID effects from Moment 1 to Moment 2 (e.g., +9.03 WPM; +7.09 accuracy points; +3.14 expressiveness units) and from Moment 1 to Moment 3 (e.g., +11.87 WPM; +9.04 accuracy points; +6.23 expressiveness units), with effect sizes around 0.42–0.47 SD for Moments 2 and 3. The paper does not use ILSA/PIRLS achievement PVs and does not report a formal missing-data strategy beyond describing attrition and exclusions; therefore, causal interpretation is limited by non-random assignment and incomplete reporting of missing-data handling. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an empirical quasi-experimental evaluation of a reading intervention using difference-in-differences and OLS with student fixed effects; it does not train or compare machine learning models, and it does not use ILSA/PIRLS achievement scores with Plausible Values. Consequently, the ML technique fields are empty and main_findings are not populated under the ML-predictive schema.
